[{"node":"security_menu_content","element":"menu_content","data":{},"elements":[{"node":"md_security_overview","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Overview","id":"security-overview","value":"# Security

Loopar is a multi-tenant framework: one process serves every tenant, so security is built into the core instead of left to each app. This page is the map of what the framework does for you, and what you still have to decide when you deploy.

| Layer | What protects it | Details |
|-------|------------------|---------|
| **Tenants** | Per-request tenant context, per-tenant database, per-tenant secrets | [Tenant isolation](#tenant-isolation) |
| **Identity** | Argon2 passwords, httpOnly JWT sessions, OAuth, two-factor authentication | [Authentication](/authentication) |
| **Authorization** | Role grants, `own` scope, deny rules, checked on every action | [Permissions](/permissions) |
| **Requests** | CSRF double-submit, action allowlist, GET-safe mutations, rate limiting | [Request protection](#request-protection) |
| **Data at rest** | Hashed or encrypted secret fields, hashed reset tokens | [Data protection](#data-protection) |
| **HTTP surface** | Security headers, upload limits, active-content and SSRF guards | [HTTP hardening](#http-hardening) |
| **Public forms** | Honeypot, spam scoring, ALTCHA proof-of-work | [Public forms](#public-forms-and-spam) |
| **First install** | Setup gate for remote installs | [Installation](#installation) |

None of this needs configuration to be on. The [production checklist](#production-checklist) at the end lists the few things that do."}},{"node":"md_security_tenants","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Tenant Isolation","id":"security-tenants","value":"## Tenant Isolation

Every request is resolved to one tenant **before** any controller runs, and that tenant travels with the request (AsyncLocalStorage). Everything below is scoped to it:

- **Database** — each tenant has its own database (`sites/<tenant>/config/db.config.json`). There is no shared table to filter by tenant, so a missing `where` can't leak another tenant's rows.
- **Signing secret** — each tenant gets a random 256-bit JWT secret, stored in `sites/<tenant>/config.json`. A session, CSRF or workspace token minted for tenant A is just an invalid signature on tenant B.
- **Encryption key** — secret fields are encrypted with a key derived per tenant (HKDF). Ciphertext copied from one tenant can't be read by another.
- **Cookies** — session cookies are named per tenant (`loopar_token_<tenant>`).
- **Cache** — permission and session cache keys are prefixed with the tenant id, in memory or in Redis.
- **Realtime** — Socket.IO connections authenticate with the same JWT and join only their tenant's namespace."}},{"node":"md_security_sessions","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Sessions","id":"security-sessions","value":"## Sessions and Cookies

- The session is a **JWT in an httpOnly cookie** — page scripts can't read it. It lasts one day and is refreshed when it gets close to expiry.
- Cookies are `SameSite=Lax` and `Secure` whenever the request is HTTPS (Loopar trusts `X-Forwarded-Proto` only from the local Caddy proxy).
- **Disabling a user ends their session.** The `disabled` flag is checked on every authenticated request and its cache is invalidated when the User is saved, so a disabled user is out on their next click — no need to wait for the token to expire.
- **Desk vs website accounts.** `System` users work in the desk; `Web` users (self sign-up, OAuth sign-up) are bounced from it. On a website domain only `Web` users can sign in, with the same error as a wrong password, so the public login can't be used to probe administrator accounts.
- **Two-factor authentication.** Any user can protect the account with an authenticator app. When it's on, *every* login path — password, Google/GitHub, cloud claim link — stops at a code step before the session is opened. See the two-factor section on [Authentication](/authentication)."}},{"node":"md_security_requests","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Request Protection","id":"security-requests","value":"## Request Protection

**Only declared actions are reachable.** A controller method is an HTTP endpoint only if it is named `action*` (login + permission required) or `publicAction*` (anonymous). Anything else is private server code.

**CSRF.** Authenticated state-changing requests must echo the `csrf-token` cookie in the `x-csrf-token` header (double-submit). The framework client does it for you.

**Workspace token.** The page load signs the workspace it was served from (`desk`, `portal`, …) and the client sends it back on every call (`X-Workspace-Token`). A browser can't claim a workspace it never loaded. It is context, not authorization — permissions are still checked per action.

**No mutations over GET.** `delete` and `bulkDelete` are refused over GET, and a controller can list more with `static postOnlyActions`:

```javascript
export default class InvoiceController extends BaseController {
  static postOnlyActions = ["approve", "void"];
}
```

**Safe redirects.** `?redirect=` return URLs after login are accepted only as same-origin paths (`/…`, never `//…` or another host).

**Rate limiting.** The anonymous auth actions — login, register, password recovery, username recovery and the two-factor code step — share a limit of **15 requests per 15 minutes per IP**. With Redis configured the counter is shared across workers."}},{"node":"md_security_data","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Data Protection","id":"security-data","value":"## Data Protection

**Passwords** are hashed with **Argon2** (`loopar.hash()` / `loopar.verifyHash()`) and never stored or returned in clear.

**Secret fields.** A `password` element has two storage modes, set with its `secret` property:

| Mode | Stored as | Use it for |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| `encrypt` *(default)* | AES-256-GCM ciphertext (`enc:v1:…`) | Credentials Loopar must send out: SMTP passwords, API keys, OAuth client secrets, git tokens |
| `hash` | Argon2 hash | Values that are only ever verified: login passwords, reset tokens |

Either way the value is **masked** (`********`) when a document is sent to the browser, saving a form without touching the field keeps the stored value, and document history never records secret values.

The encryption key is derived from the tenant's `secretKey` in `sites/<tenant>/config.json`, or from `LOOPAR_SECRET_KEY` when that env var is set (still salted per tenant). **Back up that key with the database**: without it, encrypted fields can't be decrypted.

**Password reset links** carry a random token that is stored only as a SHA-256 hash, expires in 30 minutes and works once.

**Two-factor secrets** are encrypted like any secret field; recovery codes are stored as Argon2 hashes."}},{"node":"md_security_http","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"HTTP Hardening","id":"security-http","value":"## HTTP Hardening

Every response — pages, API, assets and error pages — carries:

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `SAMEORIGIN` |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` |
| `Content-Security-Policy` | `frame-ancestors 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'` |
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` (HTTPS only) |

**Uploads** are bounded: 50 MB per file, 20 files and 10 MB per non-file field per request — one huge upload can't exhaust the memory of the process that serves every tenant.

**Active content is rejected** at upload time, on every channel (public forms, desk file manager, server-side imports): HTML, SVG, XML and JavaScript files would run in your origin if served inline, so they are refused by extension and by mime type.

**Remote imports** (adding a file by URL) only fetch `http(s)` URLs whose host does not resolve to a loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata address, so a form can't make the server read your internal network."}},{"node":"md_security_forms","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Public Forms","id":"security-forms","value":"## Public Forms and Spam

Contact forms, reviews and guest comments are open to anyone, so they get layered defenses with no external service required:

1. **Honeypot + timing** — a hidden field bots fill in, and a minimum fill time.
2. **Spam scoring** — language-agnostic signals (disposable email domains, link-heavy text, messenger funnels, known flagged senders…). Suspicious messages are stored as `Spam` without notifying anyone; obvious spam is rejected.
3. **Proof-of-work captcha** — **ALTCHA** is on by default: self-hosted, no third-party calls, no per-domain registration, single-use challenges. **Cloudflare Turnstile** can be enabled instead from Integrations.

Forms built with the Contact Form Builder go through the same server-side checks."}},{"node":"md_security_install","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Installation","id":"security-install","value":"## Installation

Before a tenant is installed, its setup wizard has to be reachable without a user. To keep a fresh server from being claimed by whoever reaches it first:

- From the **same machine or local network**, the wizard works as usual.
- From a **public IP**, it requires the **install link** printed by the CLI/TUI. Opening that link sets a short-lived setup cookie, so the wizard needs nothing else.
- Once the tenant is installed, the setup actions are revoked and the token stops working."}},{"node":"md_security_checklist","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Production Checklist","id":"security-checklist","value":"## Production Checklist

- **Serve over HTTPS** through Caddy — it enables `Secure` cookies and HSTS.
- **Keep the dev site private.** It is the control center for every tenant.
- **Turn on two-factor authentication** for every `System` user, starting with Administrator (Profile → Security).
- **Turn on scheduled, encrypted backups with a remote copy** ([Backups](/backups)). Each archive includes `sites/<tenant>/config.json` — its key decrypts the tenant's stored secrets — so keep the passphrase and the destination private.
- **Configure Redis** before running more than one worker, so rate limits and permission caches are shared.
- **Review every `publicAction*`** in your apps: they skip login, permissions and CSRF, so they must validate their own input.
- **Grant the least you need.** Prefer `own` (or `customer` for portal users) scope for user-facing documents, and keep `*:*` for administrators.
- **Keep the Debugger off in production** (the default) and revoke debug tokens you no longer use.
- **Know the way back in:** `yarn mfa-reset <tenant> <user>` turns off two-factor for a user who lost their phone and recovery codes; `yarn admin-reset <tenant> [email]` recreates the Administrator or gives it a temporary password."}}]}]
